Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1252; properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial:--without partiality.
BiblicalUsage: Adiakritos appears once, in James's portrait of the wisdom from above: it is 'without partiality, and without hypocrisy.' The word means undivided, not making distinctions between people. Heavenly wisdom does not pick favourites or play sides; it treats people the same, whether they are rich or poor, friend or stranger.
TheologicalSignificance: I won't build doctrine on a word this small — its job is to hold a sentence together, and the teaching belongs to the passage it sits in; in this case, the verse is James 3:17.
